what: Simultaneous confidence intervals for predictions in logistic regression models
title: An introduction to the mcprofile package
text: advanced example, point-wise simultaneous confidence bands computed based logistic regression model. dose-response experiment lethal effect insecticide tested. data example artificially generated, based excerpt real experiment, assuming small sample sizes.  dose-response curve modeled logistic regression model yi∼Binomial(ni,μi),ηi=log⁡(μi1−μi),ηi=β1+log⁡(xi)β2. y_{} \sim Binomial(n_{}, \mu_{}), \qquad \eta_{} = \log \left( \frac{\mu_{}}{1-\mu_{}} \right), \qquad \eta_{} = \beta_{1} + \log (x_{}) \beta_{2}. transformed parameters ϑk=∑j=1pakjβj\vartheta_{k} = \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{kj}\beta_{j} representing predictions prespecified dose levels ak2a_{k2} intercept design coefficients ak1a_{k1}. Predictions made 20 logarithmic dose values [−1,2.3][-1,2.3].  confidence bands can presented graphic shaded area around predicted curve.
code: data(toxinLD) toxinLD$logdose <- log(toxinLD$dose) ggplot(toxinLD, aes(x=logdose, y=dead/(dead+alive))) +    geom_point(size=3) mlr <- glm(cbind(dead, alive) ~ logdose, data=toxinLD, family=binomial(link="logit")) pdose <- seq(-1,2.3, length=7) cmlr <- model.matrix(~ pdose) rownames(cmlr) <- round(pdose, 2) head(cmlr) ##       (Intercept) pdose ## -1              1 -1.00 ## -0.45           1 -0.45 ## 0.1             1  0.10 ## 0.65            1  0.65 ## 1.2             1  1.20 ## 1.75            1  1.75 plr <- mcprofile(mlr, cmlr) cilr <- confint(plr)  plot(cilr) +   xlab("logit(mu)") +   ylab("log dose level") pdat <- data.frame(logdose=pdose) pdat$estimate <- mlr$family$linkinv(cilr$estimate$Estimate) pdat$lower <- mlr$family$linkinv(cilr$confint$lower) pdat$upper <- mlr$family$linkinv(cilr$confint$upper)  ggplot(toxinLD, aes(x=logdose, y=dead/(dead+alive))) +    geom_ribbon(data=pdat, aes(y=estimate, ymin=lower, ymax=upper), linewidth=0.95, fill="lightblue") +   geom_line(data=pdat, aes(y=estimate), linewidth=0.95) +   geom_point(size=3) +   ylab("Mortality rate")

title: Identifying the lethal dose of a crop protection product. — toxinLD
code: str(toxinLD) #> 'data.frame':	6 obs. of  3 variables: #>  $ dose : num  0.312 0.625 1.25 2.5 5 ... #>  $ dead : int  1 0 1 2 9 10 #>  $ alive: int  9 9 9 8 1 0  ############################################### # logistic regression on the logarithmic dose # ###############################################  toxinLD$logdose <- log(toxinLD$dose) fm <- glm(cbind(dead, alive) ~ logdose, data=toxinLD, family=binomial(link="logit"))  ############# # profiling # #############  # contrast matrix pdose <- seq(-1,2.3, length=7) CM <- model.matrix(~ pdose)  # user defined grid to construct profiles mcpgrid <- matrix(seq(-11,8,length=15), nrow=15, ncol=nrow(CM)) mc <- mcprofile(fm, CM, grid=mcpgrid) #> Warning: orglm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred #> Warning: orglm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred #> Warning: orglm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred #> Warning: orglm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred  #################################### ## confidence interval calculation # ####################################  # srdp profile ci <- confint(mc) ppdat <- data.frame(logdose=pdose) ppdat$estimate <- fm$family$linkinv(ci$estimate$Estimate) ppdat$lower <- fm$family$linkinv(ci$confint$lower) ppdat$upper <- fm$family$linkinv(ci$confint$upper) ppdat$method <- "profile"  # wald profile wci <- confint(wald(mc)) wpdat <- ppdat wpdat$estimate <- fm$family$linkinv(wci$estimate$Estimate) wpdat$lower <- fm$family$linkinv(wci$confint$lower) wpdat$upper <- fm$family$linkinv(wci$confint$upper) wpdat$method <- "wald"  # higher order approximation hci <- confint(hoa(mc)) hpdat <- ppdat hpdat$estimate <- fm$family$linkinv(hci$estimate$Estimate) hpdat$lower <- fm$family$linkinv(hci$confint$lower) hpdat$upper <- fm$family$linkinv(hci$confint$upper) hpdat$method <- "hoa"  # combine results pdat <- rbind(ppdat, wpdat, hpdat)   ##################################### # estimating the lethal dose LD(25) # #####################################  ld <- 0.25 pspf <- splinefun(ppdat$upper, pdose) pll <- pspf(ld) wspf <- splinefun(wpdat$upper, pdose) wll <- wspf(ld) hspf <- splinefun(hpdat$upper, pdose) hll <- hspf(ld)  ldest <- data.frame(limit=c(pll, wll, hll), method=c("profile","wald", "hoa"))  ################################ # plot of intervals and LD(25) # ################################  library(ggplot2) ggplot(toxinLD, aes(x=logdose, y=dead/(dead+alive))) +    geom_ribbon(data=pdat, aes(y=estimate, ymin=lower, ymax=upper,                               fill=method, colour=method, linetype=method),                alpha=0.1, linewidth=0.95) +   geom_line(data=pdat, aes(y=estimate, linetype=method), linewidth=0.95) +   geom_point(size=3) +   geom_hline(yintercept=ld, linetype=2) +   geom_segment(data=ldest, aes(x=limit, xend=limit, y=0.25, yend=-0.05,                                 linetype=method), linewidth=0.6, colour="grey2") +   ylab("Mortality rate")

title: mcprofile 1.1-0
text: hoa() now computes modified likelihood root correctly contrasts one nonzero coefficient, averages, trends Tukey-type comparisons models correlated coefficients. Previously nuisance information taken sub-block covariance matrix, correct contrasts select single coefficient. Adjusted statistics, intervals p-values change contrasts, cases much whole higher-order correction. Pairwise contrasts cell-means models (example Dunnett example vignette) nearly unaffected. hoa() also uses working weights final constrained fit, changes results slightly (1e-4) contrasts. hoa() longer discards every profile point larger data sets.

title: mcprofile 1.1-0
text: plot() failed intervals confint(..., alternative = "less"). expit() now exported generic, expit(confint(...)) transforms intervals probability scale documented. mcprofile() failed grid points lay one side estimate. mcprofile() lm objects failed data, weights formula defined inside function, data name argument mcprofile() (example CM). confint() now checks adjust alternative. misspelled alternative previously gave confusing error, silently return unrelated object called ci workspace intervals. Unambiguous abbreviations alternative = "g" now accepted. summary() validates adjust alternative way, also accepts unambiguous abbreviations. mcprofile() now gives clear error models aliased (NA) coefficients, contrast matrix wrong number columns. profile interpolated (example fewer four profile points), confint(), summary() plot() give one warning naming affected contrasts, whose results NA. Previously error message printed console without warning.

title: mcprofile 1.1-0
text: ggplot2 now imported instead attached, library(mcprofile) longer puts ggplot2 functions search path. plot() still returns ggplot objects; call library(ggplot2) modify , example + ylim(-5, 5). Profiling faster: constrained fit solves quadratic program per iteration, starting values side estimate chosen better. Requires ggplot2 3.4.0 later. plot() intervals longer uses deprecated geom_errorbarh(). citation uses bibentry(). Added test suite.
